author: high2
claim: In every reachable configuration, the unoccupied squares are exactly the squares of a monotone cell-path from (1,n) to (m,1), and a legal coin move is exactly the local path-word replacement DL by LD.
evidence: Initially the unoccupied squares, in order, are (1,n),(2,n),...,(m,n),(m,n-1),...,(m,1), a monotone path with word D^(m-1)L^(n-1). Assume the holes form such a path. A legal move in a 2-by-2 block has holes at its northeast, southeast, and southwest squares and a coin at its northwest square. Monotonicity forces those three holes to be consecutive in the order northeast, southeast, southwest, so replacing the southeast hole by the northwest hole changes the path segment DL to LD. Conversely, if a path has a DL segment, its three consecutive squares are northeast, southeast, southwest in a 2-by-2 block; the northwest square cannot lie elsewhere on the monotone path, so it is occupied, and the associated coin move is legal.

links.statement: The hole-set is a monotone path and legal moves are precisely its DL-to-LD corner flips.

glossary.D: a one-square downward step in the monotone path of empty squares
glossary.L: a one-square leftward step in the monotone path of empty squares

author: xhigh
claim: For positive integers m,n, every reachable configuration has as its empty squares the vertices of a monotone path from (1,n) to (m,1), using steps E:(i,j)->(i+1,j) and S:(i,j)->(i,j-1); a legal coin move replaces one adjacent ES corner of this empty path by SE.
evidence: Initially the empty squares are exactly the last column followed by the last row, the path E^(m-1)S^(n-1). If a coin moves from (i,j) to (i+1,j+1), the three empty squares before the move are (i,j+1),(i+1,j+1),(i+1,j), an ES corner, while after the move the empty squares in that 2-by-2 block are (i,j+1),(i,j),(i+1,j), the corresponding SE corner. All other squares are unchanged, so induction proves the claim.

links.statement: Reachable empty-square sets are monotone paths, and moves are adjacent corner swaps.

author: xhigh3
claim: In every reachable configuration, each northwest-southeast diagonal D_k = {(i,j): i-j=k}, for 1-n <= k <= m-1, contains exactly one unoccupied square.
evidence: Initially, the unoccupied squares are precisely those with i=m or j=n. For every k from 1-n through m-1, exactly one of those boundary squares satisfies i-j=k. A legal move from (i,j) to (i+1,j+1) makes (i,j) unoccupied and (i+1,j+1) occupied; these two squares have the same value of i-j. Thus a move does not change the number of unoccupied squares on any D_k. Induction on the number of legal moves proves the claim.

links.statement: Each northwest-southeast diagonal has exactly one vacancy in every reachable state.

glossary.D_k: the set of grid squares (i,j) satisfying i-j=k
glossary.k: an integer diagonal index with 1-n <= k <= m-1
